page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Flex.2-32 is a flexible virtual machine instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores with hyperthreading) and 32.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, the instance provides 64 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), AES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, features no bundled local storage, and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark data highlights exceptionally strong single-threaded CPU capabilities, placing it in the top 10% tier across Geekbench single-core (2588.0), stress-ng single-core (3428.28), gzip compression (37.62 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (16.56 GB/sec). Conversely, aggregate parallel execution scales according to its 4-vCPU hardware footprint. Multi-core performance registers in the middle 50% tier, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 6024.0, a PassMark CPU score of 9137.54, and stress-ng multi-core performance of 6845.86. Memory subsystem performance remains balanced, achieving 45.98 GB/sec read bandwidth and 33.88 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256MB uncached blocks.

With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU), VM.Standard.E6.Flex.2-32 offers high memory density relative to core count. This makes the configuration cost-efficient for workloads constrained primarily by memory capacity rather than parallel computing cores, avoiding the need to overprovision vCPUs simply to meet memory demands. A key operational tradeoff is the total reliance on remote network-attached block volumes, as no local NVMe storage is bundled.

The instance is well suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, such as Redis deployments, medium-sized in-memory databases, and web application servers handling memory-heavy worker pools. Additionally, its high single-core compute performance makes it suitable for latency-sensitive tasks like single-threaded data transformation, lightweight continuous integration builds, and small-model LLM inference.

Powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz with AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions, the instance includes one public IPv4 address, zero GPUs, and no bundled local storage. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier single-core CPU throughput, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2588.0 and gzip compression of 37.62 GB/sec, while multi-core metrics like the PassMark CPU score of 9137.54 reflect expected 4-thread scaling.
